sources.text: Zage Lab Principal Investigator Peter E. Zage, MD, PhD Peter Zage, MD, PhD, is an Associate Professor-in-Residence at UCSD and the Moores Cancer Center and is a pediatric oncologist at Rady Children's Hospital San Diego. Dr. Zage is an expert in the treatment of the pediatric solid tumors neuroblastoma and retinoblastoma, and his laboratory is focused on developing novel treatments and identifying novel targets for therapies for children with solid tumors. Read Full Bio. The primary laboratory projects in the Zage lab include studies to better understand the pathways involved in the regulation of growth factor receptor trafficking and degradation in tumor cells and their role in tumor growth and treatment response in addition to studies to identify novel therapeutic targets and novel agents to use in combination with established therapies. More about Zage lab research .

sources.text: Team Lab Team Dr. Peter E. Zage, MD, PhD ( Bio ) Dr. Zage is an Associate Professor-in-Residence at UCSD and the Moores Cancer Center and is a pediatric oncologist at Rady Children's Hospital San Diego. Dr. Zage is an expert in the treatment of the pediatric solid tumors neuroblastoma and retinoblastoma, and his laboratory is focused on developing novel treatments and identifying novel targets for therapies for children with solid tumors. Dr. Divya Subramonian, PhD : Divya is a senior research associate and laboratory manager for the Zage laboratory. Her current projects include efforts to understand the role of NME1 and histidine kinase signaling in neuroblastoma tumor cell differentiation and to evaluate the efficacy of novel therapeutic agents and combinations in mouse xenograft models of pediatric solid tumors. Dr. Christopher Le Clorennec : Christophe is a senior research associate for the Zage laboratory. His current projects include efforts to understand the role of UBE4B and growth factor receptor trafficking in neuroblastoma pathogenesis. Students & Fellows Breanna Breeding, MD : Breanna is a 3rd year fellow in pediatric hematology-oncology at Rady Children's Hospital and is currently investigating the efficacy and mechanisms of action of novel therapies directed against pediatric neural tumor stem cells. Taelor Getz : Taelor is a graduate student in the UCSD Biomedical Sciences Program and is currently exploring the targeting MYCN-mediated signaling in neuroblastoma models. Student Volunteers Amogh Chaturvedi : Amogh is a junior at Canyon Crest Academy in Carmel Valley currently volunteering in the laboratory. Erica Steen : Erica is a UCSD undergraduate student currently volunteering in the laboratory. Postdoctoral Position Available Postdoctoral Fellowship position available. Requirements: Strong background in cellular and molecular biology required. Prefer experience with in vitro and in vivo models of cancer. English language proficiency and strong publication record preferred. To Apply: Please send CV and cover letter and contact information for 3 references who are familiar with your scientific work to pzage@ucsd.edu . Please indicate specific interest and experience relevant to this position. "Generic" inquiries are not encouraged. sources.text: Contact Us PI Contact Information Peter Zage, MD, PhD Associate Professor-in-Residence, Department of Pediatrics University of California San Diego School of Medicine Moores Cancer Center, Room 5311 3855 Health Sciences Drive, Mail Code 0815 La Jolla, CA 92093-0815 Phone (office): 858-534-6494 pzage@ucsd.edu ; pzage@rchsd.org Rady Children's Hospital - San Diego Pediatric Hematology/Oncology 3020 Childrens Way, Mail Code 5035 San Diego, CA 92123-4282 Phone: 858-966-5811 Pager: 858-494-4290 Lab Mailing Address Moores Cancer Center, Room 5314-5P 3855 Health Sciences Drive, Mail Code 0815 La Jolla, CA 92093-0815 Phone: 858-534-4780 Inquiries & Requests Clinical inquiries & appointments Please visit the Rady Children's Hospital Hematology/Oncology website or call the Peckham Center for Cancer and Blood Disorders at 858-966-5811. Reprint Requests Reprints of publications can be made by request or visit the Publications page for links to selected publications. Reagent Requests Send requests to pzage@ucsd.edu . Visit the UCSD Material Transfer Agreement website regarding the MTA process. Frequently asked questions can be addressed on this site. Map and Directions Driving Directions From I-5: Exit on Genesee Avenue and go east. Turn right on Campus Point Drive. When you reach the intersection with Medical Center Drive, Shiley Eye Institute will be located to the left; Perlman Medical Offices, Jacobs Medical Center (including Thornton Pavilion) and Sulpizio Cardiovascular Center will be to the right. To get to Moores Cancer Center, turn left on Medical Center Drive and follow it around Shiley Eye Institute to Health Sciences Drive. From I-805: Exit on La Jolla Village Drive/Miramar Road, and go west. Turn right on Genesee Avenue, then turn left on Campus Point Drive. When you reach the intersection with Medical Center Drive, Shiley Eye Institute will be located to the left; Perlman Medical Offices, Jacobs Medical Center (including Thornton Pavilion) and Sulpizio Cardiovascular Center will be to the right. To get to Moores Cancer Center, turn left on Medical Center Drive and follow it around Shiley Eye Institute to Health Sciences Drive. Volunteer Opportunities in the Zage Laboratory We are always looking for driven student volunteers to engage in exciting research opportunities! Being part of cutting-edge research is a fun and valuable experience appreciated by admissions committees of medical and graduate schools as well as future employers. Please send relevant CVs or résumés, with cover letters to pzage@ucsd.edu to be reviewed as fitting opportunities become available.

sources.text: Faculty Labs The Department of Pediatrics at UC San Diego is one of the nation's premier Departments devoted to improving the understanding of disease pathogenesis in order to better diagnose, treat and prevent diseases in infants and children. Research efforts include basic and clinical science in various fields spanning the whole range of maladies. Another important goal in the Department is to build and foster the development of the next generation of research leaders in Pediatric Medicine. There has been no better time for research and training in Pediatrics than what is currently and what we predict it will be in the next decade!
